title: Unknown source probabilities left 1.7 to 14.4 percent of median linear information in eight selected worm circuit models
abstract: We tested whether mixed target inputs can separate one source release probability from unknown probabilities at other sources. Eight public worm brain maps supplied a fixed 162-neuron panel. Independent Bernoulli sites had unit positive effects. We compared known-background linear information with information after projection against all other source mean profiles. Map median retained fractions were 1.68 to 14.42 percent. The first three maps had 99 non-estimable source-map cases. All sources were estimable in maps 4 to 8, but median information still fell sharply. Rational null spaces confirmed ranks and estimable counts. Independent contact noise retained median fractions of 0.76 to 11.78 percent. Assumed direct information about other sources reduced the loss. These are conditional linear model results, not measured coding. Partial maps, unknown gains, site independence, ideal readout access and absent activity data limit use. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. Raw records and record-level arrays are excluded.

display.caption: Median linear information under known and unknown background probabilities in eight selected anatomical models. Added information is an assumed independent source measurement, not fitted biological evidence.
